body:
Do we want to display `"my query"` instead of `my query`?

If so, it'd be nice to wrap the `name` value with double quotes.

ah yes, we've mentioned this in [the related PR I made on ais](https://github.com/algolia/angular-instantsearch/pull/301#discussion_r226354923)
Isn't it a `<q>...</q>` tag IIUC ?
Yep, should be done in a q tag which displays as quotes
@tkrugg It should be in this file then: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/widgets/current-refined-values/defaultTemplates.js

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2982512/47362267-56a70f80-d6d4-11e8-824a-dd901edc5bbe.png)

So I can't find where that template rendering is tested. If I read correctly the render method is mocked so changing the default template can't break the tests?

You can test the rendering in the component itself when rendering a `query`: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/1510a9439bb22dd31eb4dc0c75bd4316a57db73d/src/components/CurrentRefinedValues/__tests__/CurrentRefinedValues-test.js

I maybe be missing something but this doesn't seem to be testing the default template neither since it's mocked.
https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/1510a9439bb22dd31eb4dc0c75bd4316a57db73d/src/components/CurrentRefinedValues/__tests__/CurrentRefinedValues-test.js#L16-L23

Right, then getting back to [the widget test file](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/1510a9439bb22dd31eb4dc0c75bd4316a57db73d/src/widgets/current-refined-values/__tests__/current-refined-values-test.js), you can pass the [default template](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/1510a9439bb22dd31eb4dc0c75bd4316a57db73d/src/widgets/current-refined-values/defaultTemplates.js) to your widget (it's already imported).
We shouldn't rely exclusively on snapshots. I think this is something we should move away from. We completely forget what we're testing.
This shouldn't be a comment but an assertion.

I agree with you. I hate snapshots, too for the same reasons.
However:
- The snapshotted thing here is a string so there is no very easy way to test it (no enzyme)
- the name of the test `it('wraps query refinements with <q>') can address the concern you have about forgetting the purpose of test
What do you think @francoischalifour ?
I ended up testing the defaultTemplate separately which I think is more consistent with the ways the concerns have been separated up to now. What do you think?
Why using `toContainEqual` on each elements rather than `isEqual` on the global array?
Since we already cover the case with facet refinements, we can focus the test only on query it will simplify it a bit.
You can test that the expected value are inside inside the string + snapshots. The intent of the test will be a bit clearer.
isEqual adds a constraint of order which I didn't think was relevant.
since I simplified the tests and removed the other refinement, I now use isEqual
There shouldn't be a space before the colon (`:`). Why are there so many spaces after the colon?

it comes from the ${computedExclude} in the returned string `${computedLabel} ${computedExclude} ${computedName} ${computedCount}`. I would change it to a regexp but I didn't think it mattered and regexp get hard to read with so many `<` `>` `/` involved.

We could write it as       `.toMatch(new RegExp("Query +: +<q>Samsu</q>"));` if you like?
Actually, the space before the colon was already the previous behavior.
